map.估算模型量化（如 FP32→INT8）的压缩比。: Estimate the compression ratio of model quantization (e.g. FP32->INT8).
map.压缩比 = 原位数 / 目标位数；模型大小(MB) ≈ 参数量 × 位数 / 8: Compression ratio = original bits / target bits; model size (MB) ~ parameter count x bits / 8 / 1024²
map.量化通过降低权重数值精度（FP32→INT8 即 4:1）直接缩小体积与带宽需求: Quantization lowers weight numeric precision (FP32->INT8 is 4:1), directly shrinking size and bandwidth needs, with clear gains on compute-limited devices. But accuracy loss shows up in metrics; models sensitive to outliers need quantization-aware training or per-channel calibration.
map.FP32→INT8 约 4× 压缩，需校准保精度。: FP32->INT8 is about 4x compression and needs calibration to preserve accuracy.
map.压缩比=量化前位数/量化后位数，如 FP32(32bit)→INT8(8bit): Compression ratio = pre-quantization bits / post-quantization bits, e.g. FP32 (32bit) -> INT8 (8bit) is theoretically 4x.
map.实际显存节省还需扣减反量化层与激活的精度开销，常略低于理论值。: Actual memory savings must also subtract the dequantization layer and activation precision overhead, often slightly below the theoretical value.
map.量化分训练后(PTQ)与量化感知训练(QAT)，后者精度损失更小。: Quantization is split into post-training (PTQ) and quantization-aware training (QAT); the latter loses less accuracy.
map.7B 模型 FP16 权重≈14GB，量化 INT8≈3.5GB(约 4× 压缩: A 7B model FP16 weights ~14GB, INT8 ~3.5GB (~4x), deployable on consumer GPUs; further INT4 ~1.75GB but with more visible accuracy loss, so verify acceptability empirically.
map.会损失一定精度，但 PTQ+校准或 QAT 可把损失压到很小；小模型/低比特(I: It loses some accuracy, but PTQ+calibration or QAT can shrink the loss greatly; small models / low bits (INT4) lose more and need validation by downstream metrics.
map.压缩比和推理速度是一回事？: Are compression ratio and inference speed the same thing?
map.相关但不等价。低比特省显存、提升访存带宽利用率，常提速；但是否真正加速还取决于硬: Related but not equivalent. Low bits save memory and improve memory-bandwidth utilization, often speeding up; but real acceleration also depends on hardware support for low-bit operators and dequantization.
map.模型量化估算（本页代码口径，十进制 MB——1MB=10⁶ 字节，非 1024²: Model quantization estimate (this page's code, decimal MB — 1MB=10⁶ bytes, not 1024² MiB): original size MB=parameters (millions)×10⁶×original bytes per parameter÷10⁶, i.e. bytes per parameter × parameters (millions) gives MB directly; new size MB uses the same formula with quantized bytes; compression ratio=original bytes per parameter ÷ quantized bytes per parameter. Validation: no strict checks; empty values count as 0; a non-finite result prompts "Some results are undefined". Grading: no fixed tiers; FP32→INT8 compresses 4× theoretically, and halving the bytes halves the size.
